newsitem.title: FRANCE: Saga to decide Oct 18 on CMB/Bollore bid.
newsitem.headline: Saga to decide Oct 18 on CMB/Bollore bid.

text.p: The board of French ports company Saga is expected to decide on October 18 the details of an agreed takeover made jointly by Bollore Technologies and the Belgian shipping group CMB NV, a spokeswoman for Bollore told Reuters on Friday.
A Saga spokeswoman confirmed that Saga had accepted the bid by Bollore and CMB but it was conditional on the approval of Saga's creditor banks which are owed around one billion francs.
Reports that Bollore and CMB would inject 125 million francs into Saga "were premature" pending the bank talks, the spokeswomen said.
But a source familiar with the negotiations said the 125 million franc recapitalisation "was not far from the reality."
Talks with Saga's banks were just starting and the outcome would determine the terms of the recapitalisation and offer.

Newspaper Le Figaro reported the bidders want Saga's bankers to write off half the medium- and long-term debt of Saga France and reschedule payments for the rest over six years as well as taking a convertible bond.
Saga had 1995 sales of some 4.5 billion francs and made a net loss of 284 million francs. First-half sales totalled 2.16 billion and the company expects to end the 1996 year in loss.
